verdict.rationale: Vercel's own docs say the CLI can be driven "through an automated system". Access tokens, which can be scoped to a single project, authenticate the CLI and REST API, and are explicitly meant to keep "jobs, tools, and workflows" constrained. The REST API/SDK and a published OpenAPI spec cover automation of projects and deployments, and Git push-to-deploy gives a CI-driven path. Missing for 10: a documented CI recipe (e.g. a CI provider guide or non-interactive token flag usage) and independent hands-on corroboration of headless CI runs.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can run the product headlessly / in CI for automation

citations.quote: With the command-line interface (CLI) you can interact with the Vercel platform using a terminal, or through an automated system
Vercel access tokens authenticate requests to the Vercel REST API and the Vercel CLI on your behalf.
This keeps jobs, tools, and workflows constrained to the projects they need rather than granting them the entire team or your full account.
Automate projects, deployments, domains, and account resources through the Vercel REST API or SDK.
Alternatively, you may opt-out by setting an environment variable: VERCEL_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1.
